title: Exact Conditional Distributions of Chi-Square-Family Statistics for Two-Way Contingency Tables, by Cell-Separable Dynamic Programming
summary: Chi-square-family statistics for two-way contingency tables are usually referred to continuous approximations, which miscalibrate because the exact both-margins-conditional law is an atomic lattice over a fibre with astronomically many tables. The paper exploits additivity of the statistic over cells and cell-wise factorization of the multivariate Fisher noncentral hypergeometric law to walk the table one cell at a time, carrying either four moment accumulators, a value-to-probability map, or one complex characteristic-function value per row-capacity state. The engine returns exact conditional moments to 5x5 at three per cell in about three seconds, exact conditional tails within its smaller reach to machine precision (e.g. 1.7e-16 on a 2x2 where a three-moment chi-square misses by 0.281), and exact simultaneous critical values for the maximum adjusted residual.

match_target.why: The user's target hint points exactly at this verification result. It is the cheapest claim that still demonstrates the paper's central contribution: a cell-separable DP that reproduces brute-force exact conditional moments of a chi-square-family statistic on a both-margins-conditioned fibre. The fibre has only 406 tables and 18 observations, so the reference enumeration is trivial and the DP run is milliseconds; no distribution map, characteristic function, or 79-billion-table lattice is needed.

tolerance.why: Rule 4 applies (unbounded error-like ratio, not a bounded score): 10% relative around 8.9e-15, i.e. roughly 8.0e-15 to 9.8e-15. The paper reports no std over repeated runs and this is not an accuracy percentage on a test set, so Rule 1 and Rules 2-3 do not apply; a faithful DP plus enumeration pair on the same fibre should land at machine precision and inside this band.

requirements.stmt: Treat the statistic as additive over cells, S = sum_ij s(O_ij, E_ij), so its moments and law accumulate by convolution as cells are added.
requirements.quote: First, every chi-square-family statistic is additive over cells

requirements.stmt: Use the both-margins-conditional law, which factorizes cell by cell as the table is built subject to running margin constraints.
requirements.quote: the margin-conditional law factorizes cell by cell as the table is built up subject to the running margin constraints

requirements.stmt: Carry four accumulators A0 = sum w, A1 = sum w s, A2 = sum w s^2, A3 = sum w s^3 per state and expand (s_new + s_partial)^r to obtain the exact first three central moments.
requirements.quote: expanding (snew + spartial)r on each step gives the exact first three central moments (mean M, variance V, third cumulant K3) of S

requirements.stmt: Walk the table one cell at a time in a fixed row-major order; the transition is a shifted slice of a dense array, not a scatter over column vectors.
requirements.quote: The fix is to walk one cell at a time

requirements.stmt: Keep the state as the row-capacity vector only: colleft is determined by the row capacities and the column total, and the last column is forced by the row capacities.
requirements.quote: it carries no information of its own, so the state stays the row-capacity vector and nothing else

requirements.stmt: Prune at each column boundary: a partial state is admissible only if its remaining row capacities can still meet the remaining column totals.
requirements.cite: Section 2.1, paragraph after the state argument
requirements.quote: a partial state is admissible if and only if its remaining row capacities can still meet the remaining column totals

requirements.stmt: Use w = 1 for all cells under the null (independence) for the reported null-fibre moments.
requirements.quote: with w the cell odds parameters (all w = 1 under independence)

requirements.stmt: For the distribution engine, carry a map from partial statistic value to probability and merge coincident atoms as each cell is convolved in.
requirements.quote: carry a map S →probability, convolving it as each cell is added and merging coincident atoms

requirements.stmt: Key atoms in exact rational arithmetic whenever the per-cell contribution is a rational function of integer counts (Pearson, likelihood ratio, rational-order power divergence); use fixed-decimal keys only for the irrational Anscombe-root atoms.
requirements.quote: the atoms can be keyed in exact rational arithmetic, removing the rounding choice entirely

requirements.stmt: Support the characteristic-function variant: accumulate φ(t) = E[exp(itS)] by the same cell-at-a-time walk with one complex number per state, and invert with the COS cosine series rather than a truncated Gil-Pelaez integral.
requirements.quote: the characteristic function φ(t) = E[exp(itS)] is accumulated by the same cell-at-a-time walk carrying one complex number per state

requirements.stmt: Verify against brute-force enumeration of the fixed-margin fibre using multiple-hypergeometric probabilities, not against Monte Carlo.
requirements.quote: enumerating the fixed-margin fibre with its multiple-hypergeometric probabilities and taking the quantile of M atom by atom

requirements.stmt: Make the per-cell summand pluggable so the same recursion returns the exact law for Pearson, likelihood-ratio and Cressie-Read members.
requirements.quote: The same engine, with the per-cell summand swapped, reproduces the exact conditional law of the Pearson, likelihood-ratio, and Cressie-Read members

requirements.stmt: Handle degenerate and zero-margin designs without special-casing failures; the vectorized engine is tested on them.
requirements.quote: across balanced, null, extreme (V = 1.2), heterogeneous, and degenerate (zero-margin) designs
